title: Neutron scattering evidence for two-dimensionally coupled spin-dimerized antiferromagnetic lattice in α-Cu2P2O7
authors: B. Ghanta, K. S. Chikara, M. Ghanathe, L. Keller, D. Voneshen, A. K. Bera
abstract: The microscopic magnetic model of the low-dimensional quantum magnet alpha-Cu2P2O7 has remained controversial. We present a comprehensive study of its magnetic ground state and excitation spectrum using temperature-dependent inelastic neutron scattering, neutron diffraction, magnetization measurements, and comprehensive spin-wave modeling. Our results unambiguously establish alpha-Cu2P2O7 as a two-dimensionally coupled spin-dimerized antiferromagnetic (AF) lattice within the bc plane, with a dominant AF exchange J2 = 7.73 meV (hereafter referred to as "intradimer exchange") and weaker exchange couplings J1, J3, and J4 in the two-dimensional lattice (hereafter referred to as "interdimer exchange"), in agreement with LDA-based density functional theory and in contrast to previous GGA+U predictions. The dominant intradimer AF exchange is found between seventh-nearest-neighbor Cu-Cu ion pairs [d(Cu-Cu) = 5.125(3) A] rather than nearest-neighbor Cu-Cu ion pairs [d(Cu-Cu) = 3.014(1) A] of the structural dimers. Weak interlayer coupling (J5 = 0.03 meV) stabilizes long-range antiferromagnetic order below TN = 25 K. We further identify a weak single-ion anisotropy, associated with the distorted CuO5 polyhedra, that opens a gap in the spin-excitation spectrum and drives a field-induced metamagnetic transition. Systematic spin-wave calculations elucidate the distinct roles of interlayer coupling J5 and anisotropy term D in producing two distinct energy gaps at different antiferromagnetic zone centers. Complementary neutron diffraction and magnetization measurements as a function of applied magnetic field uncover a previously overlooked metamagnetic transition near 13 kOe and allow construction of the magnetic phase diagram in the H-T plane.
summary: This work resolves long-standing debates about the magnetic structure of alpha-Cu2P2O7 by combining inelastic neutron scattering, magnetization measurements, and spin-wave theory. It conclusively models the material as a 2D spin-dimerized antiferromagnet, pinpointing the dominant magnetic exchange to a specific, longer-range Cu-Cu interaction. The findings provide a detailed magnetic phase diagram and elucidate the roles of weak interlayer coupling and anisotropy.
main_problem: The microscopic magnetic model of the low-dimensional quantum magnet alpha-Cu2P2O7 has been controversial, requiring clarification of the dominant magnetic exchange pathways.
main_result: The study establishes the material as a two-dimensionally coupled spin-dimerized antiferromagnetic lattice, identifying the dominant exchange interaction as occurring between seventh-nearest-neighbor Cu-Cu pairs, not nearest neighbors.
method: The research combines comprehensive experimental measurements (inelastic neutron scattering, neutron diffraction, magnetization) with advanced computational modeling (spin-wave theory, DFT).
model_or_system: The system is alpha-Cu2P2O7, modeled as a 2D coupled spin-dimerized antiferromagnetic lattice. The Hamiltonian incorporates intradimer exchange (J2), interdimer exchanges (J1, J3, J4), weak interlayer coupling (J5), and single-ion anisotropy (D).
key_observables: Energy gaps in the spin-excitation spectrum, magnetic ordering temperature (TN), metamagnetic transitions in the H-T plane, and the magnitude of various exchange couplings (J2, J5, D).
important_parameters: Dominant intradimer exchange J2 = 7.73 meV; weak interlayer coupling J5 = 0.03 meV; anisotropy D; critical magnetic field near 13 kOe.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on fitting experimental data to a spin-wave model derived from a 2D coupled dimer Hamiltonian, contrasting with previous GGA+U predictions.
figures_summary: Figures show temperature-dependent INS spectra, field-dependent neutron diffraction patterns, and simulated spin-wave spectra comparing experimental observations to theoretical models based on fitted exchange parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first presenting the experimental evidence (INS, diffraction, magnetization) to constrain the magnetic model, followed by detailed spin-wave calculations that fit the observed energy gaps and magnetic phase boundaries.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of magnetic excitations and the identification of specific, long-range exchange pathways (7th nearest neighbors) in a transition metal phosphate provides a concrete case study for understanding magnetic interactions in strongly correlated insulators.
